lesson.small: You're meeting a neighbour at a community event. They ask what you've been doing this weekend. Talk about one plan, one unfinished task and one change of schedule.
lesson.scenario: Role-play: you have a flat-viewing appointment and a separate 20-minute team call on the same afternoon. A new time conflict appears. Explain your priorities, propose a practical alternative and ask for confirmation. The AI partner should play the other person and reveal the conflict only after your first answer.
lesson.writing: Write a short message to reschedule an appointment. Explain the conflict briefly, offer one alternative, and ask for confirmation. Then rewrite one sentence using a target chunk.
lesson.note: First published as a native interactive HTML lesson. Review spacing: Day 16 (1 day), Day 14 (3 days), Day 10 (7 days).
lesson.noticing: On Saturday morning, I told a neighbour that I could fit a short coffee break in before lunch. I hadn't got around to finishing a few household tasks yet, and I was in the middle of sorting them out. Later, a colleague asked to change our call. I said, “Could we push the call back to 4 p.m.?” I had set aside time for it, so I added, “I'd appreciate it if you could confirm the new time.”
lesson.story: Tell a true 3–5-sentence story about a day when you had several things to do. Use at least two of today's chunks, but only where they fit naturally. If the story is hypothetical, clearly say so.
lesson.recovery: Start a sentence about a missed appointment. Halfway through, pretend you have forgotten the word for 'reschedule'. Keep talking: 'What I mean is, could we meet later instead?' Then try again with a different missing word. Do not restart the whole sentence.
soloQuestions: At a community event, how would you explain what you have planned for the weekend?
You have two commitments at the same time. How would you decide what to move, and what would you say to the other person?
What unfinished task have you been meaning to do, and when could you fit it in?
lesson.writingCheck: Check whether 'got around to' is followed by a noun or an -ing verb, whether 'push back' refers to a later time, and whether your request gives a clear alternative. Example structure (reveal after trying): 'Could we push our appointment back to Thursday? I can fit it in after lunch. I'd appreciate it if you could confirm.'
lesson.foundationExtra: Spelling practice: say letter names clearly, pause between groups, and practise B/V, G/J, E/I, and M/N contrasts. Never share a real password or private email address in public practice.

focus_drill: I can fit a quick call in after lunch.
